chunks: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Kurr of water: 'How much is its measure?' He said: 'When the water is three and a half hand spans in length, and likewise three and a half hand spans in breadth, and three and a half hand spans in its depth in the ground, then that is the Kurr of water.'

key_terms.أَشْبَار: Ashbar (pl. of shibr) — hand spans, the standard unit of linear measurement in classical Islamic jurisprudence, equal to the span of an open hand from thumb to little finger
key_terms.الْكُرّ: Kurr — a specific volumetric measurement in Islamic law (approx. 377–420 liters) defining the minimum quantity of water that cannot be rendered impure by contact with najasa
key_terms.عُمْق: Depth — the third dimension in the cubic definition of Kurr

ai.seo_question: What is the measurement of Kurr water according to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Abu Baseer narrates that he asked Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) about the measurement of a Kurr of water, which is the minimum quantity of water that remains pure even if impurity falls into it. The Imam defined it as a cubic volume of three and a half hand spans in length, breadth, and depth — approximately 42.875 cubic hand spans. This legal ruling was foundational for early Shia jurisprudence, defining the threshold between running/large water (which cannot be made impure) and smaller quantities requiring protection.
